"FoE Remains" is one of literally thousands of retro 2D platformers infesting Steam and lowering the average quality of all video games everywhere... and I'm not kidding. Searching for "platformers" on the Steam store page yields over 17,000 results! Is this one of the best of those? Absolutely not. This is a fan-fiction about a fan-fiction, and the fan-fiction this is a fan-fiction of is a hybrid of My Little Pony and Fallout (the post apocalyptic RPG series). These things have nothing to do with each other, but this had tremendous appeal to bronies. If you don't know what bronies are, well, congratulations for having lived a good life. A clean way to put it is that this is a fan-fiction written by balding middle aged men who really, really like TV shows made for little girls. Noah, get the boat. Anyway, bronies aside this is just a really mediocre browser/Flash game, and because you can play it in a web browser, it doesn't need to be on Steam (and for your sanity, it definitely doesn't need to be in your Steam library). Platforming is an old, mostly dead genre, and this lacklustre experience, while it doesn't have an upfront cost, isn't saving the genre... it's no surprise this failed to capture any attention from gamers in the era of immersive 3D gaming. For gameplay purposes, because the user interface for this game is mostly just 2D static text/images... it's a browser game. And we all know, Steam isn't here to compete with Chrome and Firefox. If the game can be done in a web browser, it's just not rich or compelling enough to appeal to serious gamers on PC. On the topic of visuals, the weak looking 2D retro assets seem like they'd be more at home in a browser game or a mobile app. 3D graphics accelerators hit the mainstream of PC gaming in the mid 1990's with cards like the ATI Rage and Voodoo3D, there's no excuse for such poor 2D graphics in 2025. That alone is enough to disqualify this for recommendation. The developer chose not to do the job of a real game developer and create meaningful bespoke levels, narrative based gameplay progression and so on. Instead, they decided that "Procgen IS content!" and lazily tried to use procgen algorithms to create infinite, samey, repetitive, soulless levels, because that's a lot less work. As a result of this poor decision, the game gets tired and repetitive almost immediately. Developers must learn that procgen is a terrible substitute for creating real content. It should not be used as "ez-mode" for content creation, as the developer tried to do here. This is the part of the review where we need to ask gamers to keep a straight face. This garbage was made with Adobe AIR/Flash, it's basically a 1990's browser/Flash game that's been dumped here on Steam Direct, it's polluting the place with Flash garbage, and that's a real problem. Don't laugh, they seriously published a Flash game on Steam! That's right, this developer was trying to profit from this, they wanted your money for a glorified Flash game. It's appalling, isn't it? Now on to pricing and value for gamers. This is "free" enough (not every "free" game in the "free" section is truly free, there's usually some hidden price tag), at least you won't be expected to spend any more money after you download this, but just because something is free doesn't mean it's good, and the cost of a game is more than just financial, your time is valuable too. Since free games don't contribute to your game collector badge and other profile stuff, is this a worthwhile addition to your Steam library? Not this time. This isn't worth downloading. While this won't cost you any money, you get what you pay for, and sometimes, even when the game is free, it's still not enough.

The game clearly does a few things right (or at least tries to) but it all really falls short and trips over the content bloat issue: the game seems to be a long experience for at least several hours per run but the game is just boring and the gameplay is average at best. Classic example of "I had a good idea..." and then you get content bloat (lots of unpolished/average-at-best stuff). For some reason makes me think of Cataclysm: Bright Nights. Same issue: unrealised potential and content bloat that sacrifices quality for the sake of content. I would love actually good versions of these two games: Remains and Cataclysm: Bright Nights. That is: actually polished games in all aspects and with no content bloat syndrome. For now, these two are bad games, to be honest.

Really great game. The story is awesome, the visuals and animations are good. the combat mid-late game is a bit hard. Some weapons can wipe out your health bar in like 4 shots with them being laser railguns. So you need to use med-x and or food for extra damage reduction. And the enemies to get pretty resistant so using using other drugs/food for extra damage helps kill them much faster. It's not usually too unfair though. Just make sure to optimize your damage reduction. There are lots of secret areas for more loot, and a wide variety of builds you can do. Guns, magic guns, melee, magic, explosives. The game is free so you should at least check out it. Unless you vehemently/[strike]irrationally[/strike] hate ponies.

If you like ponies and sidescrollers as well as old flash games, this is the game for you. It's got fallout theming, which makes things like the explosives you get really fun. Some of the fights even on Easy are pretty difficult, the recommended difficulty for a first playthrough - I'd suggest consulting a guide on builds before playing, it's certainly that kind of game where if you ♥♥♥♥ up your build, you'll be grinding for hours for levels to fix it. It's still a really fun game, and should run on potatoes, plus it's F R E E.

Of course someone like me would recomend this game, what do you expect? Pros: + Very huge and massive self-improving loop with many skills and different game styles you can do in game. + Dark setting very close to original Fallout Equestria. + Memorable characters/NPC and enemies. + Very good, detailed system of magic and health. + Feeling your ass whopped half of the game and then turn into a God. (Feel so good!) + The locations differ from each other and use different 2D platforming elements. Cons: - Game is too hard (Even on easy difficulty) and unforgiving. The new player be in constant loop of pain and suffer without external guides and help. - Very bad character editor (too little vanity and variety). Although it's okay, it wouldn't hurt a little more mane and tail selestion - Game notorious to have very bad optimization, because made on Adobe, so frames might drop occasionally

Been playing this game since 1.0.1, in 2020 I believe. So glad to see it on Steam now and the updates its had! I'm by far a "good gamer", so my first playthrough was on Very Easy. I also chose that for my second as that one has random skills checked, and I wanted a fun time to see what build I'd get. That player was actually v1.0.2! My third, which is the one for the current version of the game here on Steam, is Normal difficulty and Reforged. No longer can I take advantage of infinite respawns in any given level. Have to play a bit more careful- is what I would say, but honestly I took things way too slow and cautious when I was first learning the game and I'm breezing through in comparison. I love me a game that can have stupid strong enemies but it still feels balanced and fun. Tips: - Given it is a flash game, it may lag occasionally. I've found the longer I've had the game running, the slower it becomes overtime. Just save, close, and re-open the game and you'll be right as rain! - Removing slowdown isn't the only benefit that comes from reloading the game or a save. It'll also fully restore your HP. However, it won't heal the actual damage to any body parts or mana — you'll still have to visit the doc for that. [i]This exploit isn't without potential cost, though.[/i] Say you're in the middle of a floor, and reload your save. Sure, your HP will be replenished, but you'll also have to start that floor from the beginning. Due to this, it's best put to use when you're already at camp. Whenever I'm in-between floors, I personally always return to camp and save➡reload myself, so I'm less likely to immediately get pwned in the next floor. - Don't forget to level Barter! I always am selling off valuables and pre-war bits when I return to base camp to get as many caps as I can. Things get expensive, and quick. Higher barter skills come in real handy the further into the game you go! - Don't forget to level Survival! While it may not seem that important, it'll unlock the pathway to lots of useful buffs. In my first playthrough, I remember basically ignoring it (and somewhat barter, too) at first, only then to grind to level it up later when I found out all it would be able to net me. - I'm not at the point where I can test it yet but I had a major gamebreaking bug on that old release which left me unable to complete the game (it's very near the end). In case it hasn't been fixed, I'll simply denote here not to right-click / skip the text when speaking to [spoiler]the steel rangers. Dunno if it's the first or second time but just try to avoid it period.[/spoiler] Or else you'll be softlocked and have to load from an older save. It was such a devastating blow to me because by the time I realized I was stuck, my oldest save was from days earlier. So, make sure to save often and not overwrite to-file back-ups! With any luck that bug will have been patched but doesn't hurt to give a word of warning :>

十分甚至九分的好玩，之前都是官网下载的安装包来玩的，后面发现居然上架Steam了，而且存档还是互通的，这就很棒了！游戏内容还是很丰富的，难度上就算是简单难度也不会觉得很简单甚至割草，突然出现的陷阱、隐藏的敌人、致命的环境几乎处处都是你要提防的危险，武器选择还算丰富，既可以用近战武器一路砍杀过去，也可以用枪械或者魔能武器精准点杀，或者变成无所不能的魔法大师把敌人化为灰烬变成一团肉泥，也可以偷偷进行潜伏暗杀或者变成一个爆炸狂轰炸过去，甚至鱼和熊掌可以兼得，合理分配升级点数你甚至可以变成全能型选手，这游戏没有背包限制算是我喜欢的一点（选择困难症啥都想要）你可以把路上看见的一切东西都塞进自己身上把自己变成一个移动军火库（符合原著了）而且场景并不是完全死板重复的因此不容易腻，游戏中的音乐也是十分的好听，玩之前一定要把游戏的设置中的粗话过滤给关掉，看自己还有其他敌对生物说话有种别样的快乐，总之非常推荐品鉴，而且居然都玩游戏了也可以去把原著小说《辐射小马国》给看了，不过游戏和原著小说的剧情好像不一样，因此就算不看原著小说也不会影响到游戏体验
